summary: 5 corrected, 7 verified · Needs review: The 2025 loss figure (₹22,495 crore) is cited from secondary reports of the MHA Rajya Sabha reply of 11 Feb 2026. A human should swap in the direct PIB/MHA link. Some outlets quote 2024 as ₹22,848 crore in that reply.; The 2025 figure may be provisional. An I4C cheating-related subset is also quoted at ₹19,812 crore, so the exact 'reported on the portal' definition should be confirmed.; 'Golden hour' is a widely used term, but no official MHA/I4C document was retrieved that uses it. The wording is softened, and a human may want to confirm or drop it.; FIU-IND/PMLA reporting duty was verified through secondary sources. Cite PMLA Section 12 or the PML Rules directly if a primary link is wanted.; I could not retrieve the NPCI circular on UPI limits directly. The limits are from All India Radio and DD News reports of that circular.

checks.claim: Hook: cyber-fraud losses reported on the national portal in 2024 were about ₹22,845 crore
checks.note: 2024 figure verified (₹22,845.73 crore, Lok Sabha). Newer 2025 figure of ₹22,495 crore (MHA Rajya Sabha reply, 11 Feb 2026) now used for the hook, with 2024 kept as comparison.
Telangana Today / Lok Sabha reply: ₹22,845.73 crore in 2024, about 206% above 2023 (₹7,465 crore)

checks.claim: UPI handled about 186 billion transactions in FY2024-25
checks.note: PIB/NPCI: FY2024-25 was 18,586.60 crore (about 186 billion), but newer FY2025-26 is 24,161.69 crore (about 242 billion). Updated to FY2025-26.

checks.claim: MuleHunter.AI announced by RBI Innovation Hub in December 2024
checks.note: Business Standard, Dec 2024: RBIH launched MuleHunter.AI; Governor asked banks to collaborate on it

checks.claim: RBI Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management, July 2024
checks.note: AZB: RBI issued separate Master Directions for banks and NBFCs on 15 July 2024

checks.claim: NPCI general UPI per-transaction limit is ₹1 lakh with higher limits for specific categories
checks.note: AIR: since 15 Sep 2025 P2M limits in specified categories are ₹5 lakh per transaction (₹10 lakh a day), P2P stays at ₹1 lakh a day. Myth explanation updated.

checks.claim: 1930 helpline and cybercrime.gov.in are the official reporting routes
checks.note: PIB: National Cyber Crime Data; 1930 operationalised to lodge online cyber complaints

checks.claim: MHA stresses reporting within the 'golden hour'
checks.note: MHA reply confirms CFCFRMS is for immediate reporting to stop siphoning of funds. 'Golden hour' appears only in non-official sources, so attribution to MHA removed and wording softened.

checks.claim: Banks must report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND under PMLA
checks.note: IIBF: banks must escalate suspicious transactions to FIU-IND under PMLA 2002 and the PML Rules
PIB: Act enacted 11 Aug 2023; DPDP Rules 2025 notified 14 Nov 2025 with phased compliance (full effect by about May 2027)
No listed employers appeared. Phrases like 'our rails', 'our accounts' and 'accounts we opened' were changed to 'the bank's' so the scenario reads as a composite.

checks.claim: Illustrative model arithmetic (₹2.8 crore, 1,200 hours, ₹6 lakh, ₹8.4 lakh, ₹14.4 lakh a month, ₹1.7 crore a year, about 70%)
checks.note: Recomputed: 40×50,000×14 = ₹2.8 crore; 800×1.5×₹500 = ₹6 lakh; 3% of ₹2.8 crore = ₹8.4 lakh; ₹14.4 lakh×12 = ₹1.73 crore; net about ₹0.73 crore. All labelled as an illustrative model.
